title: PE header and completion checks
description: Computes the necessary PE header prefix, checks bounded PE32 and PE32+ structure against the declared file length, and requires agreement between HTTP and file completion.

topics.title: Load shared byte and filename helpers
topics.description: The relative load supplies byte slicing, numeric octets, filename selection and shared limits in the PEFileDisguise module. Main obtains these through its load of pe.

ranges.code: @load ./filename

topics.title: Export the PE classification interface
topics.description: pe_format accepts retained prefix bytes and the declared object length, returning pe32, pe32plus or an empty result. Its actual definition performs the field and extent checks.

ranges.code: global pe_format: function(prefix: string, declared: count): string;

links.label: Return a format to prefix collection

topics.title: Export the completion predicate
topics.description: completion_ok takes both completion flags, the bad flag and observed, total and declared counts. Its actual definition returns the conjunction consumed by finish in main.

ranges.code: global completion_ok: function(http_done: bool, file_done: bool, bad: bool, seen: count, total: count, declared: count): bool;

topics.title: Decode an unsigned little endian field
topics.description: le selects width bytes at zero based offset with part, then passes T to bytestring_to_count for little endian order. The PE fields read below use this helper, including the four byte DOS pointer and two byte COFF fields.

ranges.code:
function le(s: string, offset: count, width: count): count
{ return bytestring_to_count(part(s,offset,width),T); }

links: Read the DOS pointer with le

topics.title: Request the DOS header first
topics.description: needed returns 64 until the retained prefix contains the fixed DOS header. Main treats the count as the next required prefix extent and copies only enough bytes to reach it.

links.label: Return the next required extent to the cursor

topics.title: Require MZ before extending the prefix
topics.description: The first two bytes must be MZ. Otherwise needed returns max_prefix_bytes+1, a sentinel that main rejects using its cap guard.

ranges.code: if ( part(s,0,2)!="MZ" ) return max_prefix_bytes+1;

links.label: Read the cap used for the sentinel
Reject a need beyond the cap

topics.title: Bound the DOS pointer and COFF extent
topics.description: The four byte little endian e_lfanew field at offset 60 gives nt. A pointer below 64 or a signature plus COFF extent nt+24 above the prefix cap returns the oversized sentinel.

ranges.code:
local nt=le(s,60,4);
if ( nt<64 || nt+24>max_prefix_bytes ) return max_prefix_bytes+1;

links: Decode e_lfanew in little endian order

topics.title: Request the signature and COFF header
topics.description: If the retained prefix has not reached nt+24, needed returns that extent. This lets main collect the fields needed to size the optional header and section table before asking for those later bytes.

ranges.code: if ( |s|<nt+24 ) return nt+24;

links.label: Continue prefix collection to the COFF extent

topics.title: Request optional header and section entries
topics.description: The next extent is nt+24 plus SizeOfOptionalHeader and 40 times NumberOfSections. le reads those two COFF fields at nt+20 and nt+6. Main bounds this requested extent before copying or classifying.

ranges.code: return nt+24+le(s,nt+20,2)+40*le(s,nt+6,2);

links.label: Classify once the full extent is present

topics.title: Enter bounded PE classification
topics.description: pe_format takes prefix and declared. It first requires a declared length within max_object_bytes, at least 64 retained bytes and an MZ signature. Failure returns an empty result, which main marks as a rejected context.

links.label: Use the returned format or empty result

topics.title: Require the NT signature within the prefix
topics.description: The DOS pointer is decoded at offset 60. nt must be at least 64 and nt+24 must fit the retained prefix; the four bytes at nt must equal PE followed by two NUL bytes.

ranges.code:
local nt=le(prefix,60,4);
if ( nt<64 || nt+24>|prefix| || part(prefix,nt,4)!="PE\x00\x00" ) return "";

links.label: Read the exact NT signature bytes

topics.title: Read machine sections and optional size
topics.description: The COFF header supplies Machine at nt+4, NumberOfSections at nt+6 and SizeOfOptionalHeader at nt+20. These little endian fields select the accepted format and locate the section table.

topics.title: Locate the complete section table extent
topics.description: The optional header starts at nt+24. table_end adds its declared size and 40 bytes per section entry, defining the last header byte required for the following structural checks.

ranges.code: local opt=nt+24; local table_end=opt+optsize+40*sections;

topics.title: Require a bounded nonempty section table
topics.description: The section count must be 1 through 96. table_end must fit the prefix cap, the retained byte string and the declared object length. These predicates bound subsequent section field reads against all three extents.

ranges.code: if ( sections==0 || sections>max_sections || table_end>max_prefix_bytes || table_end>|prefix| || table_end>declared ) return "";

topics.title: Read the optional header magic
topics.description: The two byte magic at opt is decoded with le. fixed and format are assigned by the accepted machine and magic pairs immediately below.

ranges.code: local magic=le(prefix,opt,2); local fixed: count; local format: string;

topics.title: Select the i386 PE32 pair
topics.description: Machine 0x14c paired with magic 0x10b sets fixed=96 and format=pe32. fixed locates NumberOfRvaAndSizes and the start of data directory entries for this format.

ranges.code: if ( machine==0x14c && magic==0x10b ) { fixed=96; format="pe32"; }

topics.title: Select the AMD64 or ARM64 PE32+ pair
topics.description: Machine 0x8664 or 0xaa64 paired with magic 0x20b sets fixed=112 and format=pe32plus. Main renders the accepted result as PE32+ in the Notice.

ranges.code: else if ( (machine==0x8664 || machine==0xaa64) && magic==0x20b ) { fixed=112; format="pe32plus"; }

links.label: Render the classifier result in the Notice

topics.title: Reject other machine and magic pairs
topics.description: The else branch returns an empty string unless one of the preceding pairs assigned a format. Machine and magic must agree with a supported pair.

ranges.code: else return "";

topics.title: Fit the advertised directories in the optional header
topics.description: optsize must contain fixed bytes plus eight bytes for each advertised directory. The count at opt+fixed-4 must be at most 16. The inequality permits additional optional header padding while requiring all advertised directory entries to fit.

ranges.code: if ( optsize<fixed || fixed+8*le(prefix,opt+fixed-4,4)>optsize || le(prefix,opt+fixed-4,4)>16 ) return "";

topics.title: Read SizeOfHeaders and FileAlignment
topics.description: le reads SizeOfHeaders at opt+60 and FileAlignment at opt+36. The next guard compares the header extent with the section table and declared object length.

ranges.code:
local headers=le(prefix,opt+60,4);
local alignment=le(prefix,opt+36,4);

links: Decode header size and file alignment

topics.title: Require an aligned header extent
topics.description: SizeOfHeaders must contain table_end and fit declared. FileAlignment must be nonzero, and SizeOfHeaders must be divisible by that alignment. The same alignment constrains nonempty section raw offsets.

ranges.code: if ( headers<table_end || headers>declared || alignment==0 || headers%alignment!=0 ) return "";

topics.title: Track previously accepted raw extents
topics.description: starts and ends are parallel vectors of raw file intervals. The loop visits each of the bounded section entries using i, enabling overlap checks against every previously accepted nonempty interval.

topics.title: Read each section raw file interval
topics.description: Each section entry begins at opt+optsize+40*i. le reads SizeOfRawData at entry+16 and PointerToRawData at entry+20. These are byte extents in the declared file.

ranges.code:
local sec=opt+optsize+40*i;
local size=le(prefix,sec+16,4); local start=le(prefix,sec+20,4);

links: Decode raw section size and offset

topics.title: Check raw extents for sections with bytes
topics.description: Only a positive SizeOfRawData enters the raw extent checks and interval tracking. A zero size section proceeds to the next entry without adding an interval.

ranges.code: if ( size>0 )

topics.title: Fit aligned section bytes after headers
topics.description: A nonempty raw section starts at or after SizeOfHeaders and at or before declared. Its size must fit declared-start and its start must be divisible by FileAlignment. The subtraction bounds the end without requiring a read of section contents.

ranges.code: if ( start<headers || start>declared || size>declared-start || start%alignment!=0 ) return "";

topics.title: Require disjoint nonempty raw intervals
topics.description: For every accepted prior interval, start<ends[j] and start+size>starts[j] identifies overlap. Touching endpoints are accepted, while an actual shared byte interval returns an empty result.

ranges.code: for ( j in ends ) if ( start<ends[j] && start+size>starts[j] ) return "";

topics.title: Remember the accepted interval
topics.description: The raw start and exclusive end enter parallel vectors for later comparisons. Every following nonempty section is checked against these intervals.

ranges.code: starts+=start; ends+=start+size;

topics.title: Advance to the next section entry
topics.description: Incrementing i visits the next 40 byte entry until the bounded section count is exhausted. Empty sections also take this increment.

topics.title: Check the certificate directory when advertised
topics.description: A directory count greater than four includes directory index four. Only then does the classifier read the certificate file offset and size.

ranges.code: if ( le(prefix,opt+fixed-4,4)>4 )

topics.title: Read certificate file offset and size
topics.description: The two four byte fields at opt+fixed+32 and +36 give the certificate file offset and size. The offset addresses certificate bytes directly in the file.

ranges.code: local cert=le(prefix,opt+fixed+32,4); local csize=le(prefix,opt+fixed+36,4);

topics.title: Fit the certificate extent in the declared file
topics.description: Certificate offset and size must either both be zero or both be nonzero. The offset must fit declared, and size must fit declared-cert. This is an extent predicate on directory fields.

ranges.code: if ( (cert==0)!=(csize==0) || cert>declared || csize>declared-cert ) return "";

topics.title: Return the accepted format
topics.description: The surviving format is pe32 or pe32plus and becomes x$format in main. Trailing overlay bytes remain compatible because these structural predicates bound each advertised section and certificate extent within declared while allowing bytes after those extents.

ranges.code: return format;

links.label: Store the returned format and release prefix bytes

topics.title: Require both completions and exact byte agreement
topics.description: completion_ok returns T only when http_done and file_done are both T, bad is F, and seen and total each equal declared. Main calls this after its own completion gates and combines it with a nonempty format before emitting the Notice.

ranges.code:
function completion_ok(http_done: bool, file_done: bool, bad: bool, seen: count, total: count, declared: count): bool
{ return http_done && file_done && ! bad && seen==declared && total==declared; }

links.label: Use this boolean with the stored format
